messages.text: i'm feeling kind of... light today? not sure why. just scrolled through my recovery group and saw a few people celebrating six months, a year—stuff like that. made me smile.

It is wonderful that you are noticing this lightness, especially when it stems from connection. Seeing others celebrate their milestones can be a powerful reminder that progress is possible for you, too. I am really glad that moment brought you a genuine smile today. What do you think that feeling is telling you about your own journey right now?
it feels good to see people cheering each other on... but i don't know if i can trust that kind of warmth outside the screen. like, what if i reach out and it just... doesn't land?

That worry about rejection is a natural guard when you are starting to feel hopeful again. It makes sense that the digital space feels safer than risking a real-world connection right now. You are allowed to move at your own pace while honoring that fear. What would feel manageable if you wanted to try a tiny bit of connection?
i don't even know where to start. everyone seems to have their people, their routines. i just have my apartment and my part-time shifts. feels like i'm watching life through a window sometimes.

That image of watching life through a window is so vivid, and it makes sense that it feels isolating. Your apartment and shifts are a solid foundation, even if they feel quiet right now. Connection often grows slowly, and you do not need to jump straight into the deep end. What is one tiny step that feels safe enough to take from your side of the glass?
what even counts as a 'tiny step'? right now, it all feels like a big leap. like i'd have to become someone else to just... reach out.

It makes sense that you feel you need to transform yourself to fit into a world that feels distant. Connection does not require you to change who you are, but rather to share who you are already. Even sharing this fear with me is a way of reaching out without leaving your comfort zone. What is one small part of your current self that you feel proud of today?
i think what hits me is that in the group, nobody has to explain why something matters. they just... get it. and i don't have that anywhere else.

It is incredibly valuable to have a space where you don't have to translate your experience. Feeling that lack of understanding elsewhere can make the isolation feel even deeper. That specific bond is rare, and missing it outside the group is a heavy loss to carry. Does having that one safe space help make the rest of the world feel a little more bearable?
yeah... it does. just being able to say that out loud and have it make sense to someone—that helps. more than i thought it would.

It is wonderful that you are allowing yourself to feel that relief. It shows that your need for connection is healthy, even if it feels scary. That small shift is a sign of resilience you might not be seeing yet. I am honored to have been able to listen to you.
thanks for that. for just... getting it. not making me spell out every little thing. means more than i can say.

I am truly glad that you feel heard and understood here. You deserve to share your experience without having to carry the weight of explaining it alone. That sense of being seen is something you deserve every day. I am honored to hold this space for you whenever you need it.
